September, 1992   Page Reply


 How to write to us...02     -
 John Hall............03    06
 Phil Parnell.........07    17
 Vincent L. Jacks.....25    30
 T.J. Livett..........37    40
 Graham Yeardley......41    43
 Malcolm Perry........45     -
 Alex Morgan..........49    50

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: John Hall, BOURNEMOUTH

Dear Brian

I was so dismayed to read of the
financial problems you have with
OUTLET at the present time. I
look forward very much to rec-
eiving my disks each month and
would be very sorry indeed if
they came to an end. I see from
this months letters that you are
receiving many and varied
suggestions to alleviate your
problems.

Your suggetion to increase the
cost of OUTLET is in my  opinion
one of  the  soundest  ideas  to
implement immediately.  I would
suggest however  that  you  make


the increase `1.00 instead of
50p.It will still represent ex-
tremely good value each month
The idea of a "Hardship" dis-
count is in the circumstances
extremely generous and to be
applauded and I hope it would
not be abused. Here's hoping
things will rapidly improve.

Next, may I ask if any of your
readers has succesfully managed
to get a composite video output
from a Spectrum +3? If they
have, will they please share the
details.

Sorry if I've rambled on a bit.
I appreciate all your efforts
each month and would hate to see
the demise of OUTLET.

Incidentally, did you know that
S & SC magazine is being
incorporated into FORMAT in the
very near future according to
the editorial in this months
magazine?

All the best.

           John Hall

Brian Cavers to John Hall


Thanks, John.

Details of how to get composite
video from a +3 are in Simon
Greenfields letter in OUTLETTERS
(More Mail) in OUTLET 43 but you
would need to do some soldering.

Yes, I had heard about S&SC and
I understand outstanding subs
will be honoured.

                      - Brian

From: P. PARNELL, LANCASHIRE

Dear OUTLET,

I have a few more questions and
also a bit of information. In
connection with the Tasword +3
screen font and addresses I
wrote to Tasman with a few
questions on loading new fonts
when I ordered a new copy of
Tasword +3 ( I spilled wine all
over my copy, which promptly
dried into a sticky mess and
ruined the disk) This is what
they came back with.

"Dear Mr Parnell,

Thank you for your letter. The
64 character per line screen

fonts used by TW+3 are stored
within the program and as such
they can be modified. However,
this can only be done by dir-
ectly poking the machine code
program to modify the existing
character patterns. I regret it
is not possible to load some
existing screen fonts.


The 64cpl character pattern
table is edited by directly
poking the machine code program
i.e. by entering BASIC after
loading Tasword and executing a
series of POKE commands to
modify a character pattern. To
do this however you will need
some programming knowledge.

The character pattern starts at
address 53504 decimal and each
character consists of an 8 block
giving 8 by 8 dots per charact-
er. However, only the lower 4
bits of each byte are used. To
calculate the location of each
character use the formula:

start address + (8* ASCII value
of character)

For example, the formula for the
location of character pattern A
(decimal 65) is:

 start address   53504 +
 (8*65) =   54024
 end   address   53504 +
 (8*65+7)=  54031


To modify the character pattern
you will need to execute 8 POKE
commands from start to end
inclusive."
             Yours sincerely,
             Paul Monico

      TASMAN SOFTWARE LTD
I hope this clarifies matters a
little.I tried to load the mini-
chars into the program but fail-
ed miserably and so it seems I
will need to do what they rec-
ommend but it seems to me to be
an incredibly tedious method.
All those pokes for each char-
acter! AAAARRRGGHHH!!!! I don't
suppose you or someone out there
could come up with a bit of
BASIC or code that will do this?
(Holds his breath in hope!)

At least it will only need to be
done once as you can then save a
working copy that will have the
new char set already installed.

Just a little tip for all those
+3 owners out there who are sick
of the crappy sound from their
machine. It really stems from
the 48K Speccy method of boost-
ing the sound. Just remove any
tapes from your tape deck, press
play and remove the ear lead
from the deck. The +3 tends to
distort the tunes/sound on the
base end of the sound range. As
tape decks tend to have a
"tinny" sound from its built in
speaker it balances out the
distortion to a good degree. Not
perfect, but if you balance the


sound from the TV and the sound
from the tape deck correctly
then you can get a much better
sound.

I noticed on the label on front
of the OUTLET disk that you can
print a copyright symbol. How do
you do this on your printer? I
am having difficulty as both
EPSON and IBM character sets
have no copyright symbol in any
of their character sets, at
least not in my printer manual
they haven't. Is this just my
printer (Amstrad DMP 4000) or do
you have a method?

I notice that you have modified
the BLAST IT so that it prints
out. The only thing is that it

prints triple line spaces and
prints out VERY jerkily in
spasms. I thought you might like
to know. I have updated the
printout I gave you with all the
more pertinent letters from the
OUTLETTERS section. I have
enclosed a copy for your
personal use. Have you got
anywhere with the conversion for
OUTLET readers?

I thought I might mention that I
have found a source of very
cheap 3" disks. I don't know if
they are branded or not but he
is only charging `7.50 for 10
disks plus p+p. I seem to have
lost the name of the vendor but
you can always put something
like "The proprietor" or some


such. The address is (minus
name)

2 Service bays, Stow, Harlow,
ESSEX CM20 3AB



I have noticed that there is an
error in the "ADDPRINT" program
on OUTLET 60. It stops with an
error report "8 End of file
4500:2". This may just be my set
up but I generally get this
error if the FORMAT LPRINT "U"
command has not been present in
the program. I added it to the
beginning of 4500 and all was
O.K. after this but I suppose it
could have been added to 8800
equally as well.

I have been reading through some
past OUTLETTERS and keep
noticing the mention of another
magazine (disk?) called FORMAT.
What is this publication? Are
they still in business? If they
are can anyone supply me with
their address?

I noticed that some readers have
mentioned about the placing of
CP/M P.D in the Addenders
section of OUTLET. I know that
many readers may not have this
Utility but maybe they would get
it if there was more software
available for it? As I mentioned
last month there is a huge
amount of P.D about for this
utility almost tailor made for
the +3 (on 3" disk). I for one


would welcome its addition to
OUTLET. What do the rest of you
lot out there think?

All the best

           P.Parnell

P.S D.I.C.E or any of the other
alternatives from any company
you care to name does not save
to drive B. Catloader is the
only utility I know of that does
so.

Brian Cavers to P. Parnell

The answer from Tasman about not
being able to load character
sets in Tasword +3 is, to put it
bluntly, a load of cobblers. At
least you got a detailed reply
and they meant well (Tasman have
an excellent reputation for user
support and help) but in this
case Paul Monico is wrong.

In addition, the address he gave
you is wrong and should be...

         53248 + (8*65)

The character set does start at
53504 but one has to calculate
from a base address of 53248
because the first 31 codes are
not real characters.

I was amazed that you appear to
have been working with your only
and original Tasword +3 disc! It
is always advisable to make a
working copy and keep the orig-
inal as a back up. Tasword +3 is
quite expensive to replace!

MINICHARS W (OUTLET 23) is a
WORDMASTER character set if I
remember rightly (hence the W).
It does not work in Tasword +3.

MINICHARS 2, 3 and 4 all work in
Tasword +3 though and, since I
don't think they have ever been
published in our +3 OUTLET, I am
including them all in this month
in the ADDENDERS section.

This is what you do...

First, make a copy of your Tas+3
disc. Use CATLOADER (OUTLET 33)
or the +3 COPY command as on
Page 159 of the manual.

Load Tasword +3.

Enter B to get into BASIC.

Put this month's OUTLET in the
drive (check which side that the
MINICHARS files are on as I'm
not sure at this time.

Enter...

25 LOAD "MINICHAR.2" CODE 53504

Enter...

GO TO 25

The minichars should load and
Tasword +3 should run so you can
enter the text editor and see if
you like the characters.

Go back to BASIC and alter line
25 to "MINICHAR.3" and enter
GO TO 25 again. After checking
the appearance of the text do
the same with "MINICHAR.4". You
can go back to look at the
others until you decide which
you prefer.Once you have decided
then enter BASIC, put your
working copy of Tasword +3 in
the drive and enter...

       SAVE "DISK" LINE 20

My early copy uses the filename
"RUN" instead of "DISC". I can't

believe that Tasman haven't
altered that to "DISK" on later
versions else you cannot boot
it!

Finally, copy the MINICHARS of
your choice from the OUTLET disc
to your Tasword +3 working copy
disc. It should thereafter load
in automatically.

Let me know if you have any
trouble. The only thing I can
think of is if Tasman have
changed Tasword +3 in some way
since I got my copy.

I tried your idea to feed the
sound through the cassette
player. It worked on mine but it
may not work on all models.

Although it sounds faint and
tinny on my set up at least it
gives me a useful extra method
of monitoring sound when I am
using the TV with another
computer (e.g., when duplicating
+3 discs I have a BEEP sound in
between discs).

Regarding the copyright sign on
our discs, it may sound strange
but I don't have any labels here
(I'm working from home) and I
can't find out for a few days
which will be too late for this
deadline! However,there are only
two possiblities I can think of.

1.It may not be a copyright sign
but a small c in brackets: (c),
possibly in subscript or super-
script(see your printer manual).

2.The symbol may be printed with
graphic codes. (ESC * and ESC K,
Y and Z in your printer manual).

I favour No.1 because graphics
are relatively slow and we have
to print a lot! Sorry to be so
vague but I can't get in touch
with Ron before finishing these
letters (Ron produces the discs
and labels).

It is extraordinary that your +3
print out from BLAST IT with
triple line spacing. The program
simply LPRINTs single characters
and uses NO special codes. It
does seem your machine is faulty
in some way. What do you get if
you simply enter LPRINT "ONE":
LPRINT TWO", etc.? Triple line
spacing?!!

FORMAT magazine is `1.25 from
FORMAT PUBLICATIONS, 34 Bourton
Road, Gloucester, GL4 0LE

ROM INDEX is taking up all of
the spare space on the +3 disc
at the moment but I do have some
CP/M software which I hope one
day to include in OUTLET.

                      - Brian

From:  Mr.V.L. Jacks, LONDON

Dear Ron and Brian,

I wonder if you would be kind
enough to help me out with some
problems (yet again).
I recently ordered some back
issues of OUTLET (28, 35 and
48). Issue No. 48 is running
fine but the other two are
causing problems.

I can't load the CODE files,
EDITORIAL, OUTLETTERS, etc. I
keep getting an ERROR MESSAGE -
INVALID FILENAME 300:1 300:3.
I've tried loading them in 48K
mode and 128K mode but they
refuse to load. I've enclosed
the discs for you to look at.

I think the ERROR occurs due to
the fact that the filenames are
longer than the standard 10
characters permitted on the
Speccy. Could you please change
the filenames to a shorter
length and also the line of
BASIC at 300? I would like to
read some of the older
Editorials and Outletters.

My second problem: I used the
OMNIVAC utility on Tasword Two
and I now get very strange ERROR
messages - INVALID PARAMETER and
NUMBER TOO BIG. Luckily, I kept
an original copy of the program
and was able to send this text-
file to you. The other thing
that happens is when I try to
load one of my old textfiles it

loads in corrupted, so much so
that there are about 300 lines
of absolute rubbish on the
screen. Can you help here?

I've enclosed the offending
program as RUN and TASCODE.I've
also enclosed the running copy
of Tasword 2 as TASWORD 2 and
TASWORD, hoping that you are
able to help and also my thanks.
My Speccy is a 128K +2 (grey
Model) with Plus D fitted with
Uni-Dos and Single Drive (80
tracks DSDD).

I've been trying to use your
CODELINE program to put code
into REM's (what else)? However,
I've not been very successful
with my attempts.

Perhaps what I'm trying to do is
wrong and that's why it doesn't
work. I loaded the program and
made a header called FONT, then
I loaded a code file which are
fonts (Fnt_128) CODE 48384,768.
It loaded OK and confirmed that
this has happened. It then went
back to the main menu and the
command line at the bottom of
the menu said - NO CODE LOADED.
I tried transferring the code to
the REM and could even list it
to make sure it was there, but
the message - NO CODE LOADED
happened. Am I using the program
in the wrong manner? Simply,
what I'm trying to do is put my
favourite font sets into REMS so
that I can merge them into
programs with a GOSUB call.

Also, there is another program
on one of my back issue discs
called REM-MAKER. Apart from
making REMS, what are you
supposed to do with after that?
How do you put code into it?

I know that this may all sound
rather stupid, but then I'm a
rather stupid and confused
person. Please help.

        Yours Sincerely,

          V.L. Jacks

Brian Cavers to V.L. Jacks

I am told we have automatically
sent you replacement discs but I
now see that the problem is not
with the discs but your UNIDOS.
It appears this has some strange
limitation on the filenames and
cannot accept Sinclair tokens!
Quite why the author of UNIDOS
has done this I do not know as
it means that some software you
buy will not work. We obviously
cannot spend time producing
special versions of OUTLET for
individuals to order so you need
to remove your UNIDOS chip and
restore the original temporarily
so you can either print the text
files or rename them to end in
".#".

If you rename them (use the +D
command ERASE d1"NAME" TO "NEW")
make sure the ".#" is ALWAYS the
9th and 10th character by
inserting spaces if necessary.
You can then load the files in
later issues or rename the DATA
at line 30. An easier way might
be to save the files to tape and
reload them to disc.

I'm sorry we can't do this for
you but you appreciate OUTLET is
a commercial venture and cannot
afford to spare the time or be
responsible for the limitations
of other companies' software (as
in UNIDOS).The filenames we used
are perfectly valid Spectrum
names using the Sinclair token
"CODE" (one byte).

OMNIVAC has a slight bug in that
it puts a VAL "" into any DEF FN
command brackets. I've got a
strange idea that someone cured
this problem but I can find no
record of it! Anyone remember?

Anyway, in Tasword 2, edit line
7000 and alter it by deleting
the first VAL "" in the line...

7000 DEF FN p(x VAL"")=PEEK x+
     VAL" 256"*PEEK (x+SGN PI)

so it reads...

7000 DEF FN p(x)=PEEK x+VAL"256"
     * peek (x+SGN PI)

It will then work alright and
you can resave it.

I have to apologize for CODELINE
as it does have a bug. I cannot
get it to work either. I think
the problem may be something to
do some of the code that the
author Cliff Jackson uses that
does not work on the +D. I seem
to remember another program that
gave the same trouble. I cannot
understand why I didn't spot the
fault in the original CODELINE.
A new version of CODELINE was in
Issue 58 but this still has the
same bug. I do not alway check
ADD-ENDER programs (which is why
they are ADD-ENDERS) so I can
see why this must have got in
without my seeing the bug.In any
event I do not see how it could
be used for a font even if it
worked. I can only offer you a
refund or replacement.

If you want to replace the issue
with another I recommend Issue 7
which has REMSTORE. This is far
easier to use, is guaranteed to
work because I have used it
thousands of times and can deal
with fonts. Its only weakness is
that any code ending in a zero
or zeros will not have those
zeros stored so one needs to add
an odd spare byte of any value.
In practice,not one in a hundred
is of this type and I can barely
remember one. REMSTORE is the
program used to store all OUTLET
program code apart from very
large blocks and so is in use
regularly.

I'm sorry also REM-MAKER gives
no explanation as to its use. It

was intended for programmers who
already know how to put code in
REMs I assume. Again, it is not
ideal for fonts.

Your best be is REMSTORE. It can
run code within the REM or move
it first to any place in memory.
If you use it for fonts then you
want to use the option to move
it to a place in memory because
as I am sure you know, you need
to alter the system variable
CHARS when using fonts on the
Spectrum.If you don't know about
this then write again and I will
explain it. However, briefly,you
need to enter POKE 23606,0:
POKE 23607,188 if you use the
address 48384 mentioned in your
letter.

No, your letter doesn't sound
stupid. We are all learning. I
don't think I'll learn all there
is to know about the Spectrum if
I use it for the next 25 years!

Regarding the (unpublished) P.S.
to your letter, you have to
appreciate that I cannot give
free private advice by mail -
especially as lengthy as this
reply - because I simply could
not cope with the workload. I
have spent two hours on your
letter alone. No, we can only
answer computing queries and the
like in OUTLETTERS. The time I
spent is paid for indirectly
because it enhances the magazine
and helps other users so more
people buy OUTLET!
                     - Brian.

From: T.J. Livett, LICHFIELD


Dear Ron and Brian Cavers,

I am just writing in admiration
of Robert Frosdick's brilliant
3D Bully-Embassy program in
OUTLET No. 59. It was cleverly
thought out and most of all very
addictive.

After going through the 26 rooms
I was a little disappointed only
to receive a spinning trophy and
a "well done" message; and I'm
not sure of the significance of
the boxes in both rooms 14 and
24. But on the whole - very well
done.In case you haven't spotted
it, you can SAVE this to tape...

After 'Bully-Embassy' has LOADed
from OUTLET and you have pressed
RUN to start the game, leave the
flashing bar on Interface II
then press BREAK and then very
quickly touch the RESET button,
and you will see the message,
"Please type in the game title
and press ENTER".

Do you have a utility amongst
your bank of public domain
programs that can print out
Garry Rowland's PFN print system
program (OUTLET 59) direct to a
printer rather than dump a
portion of the screen? Could you
please let me know if you have
such a routine. If so, I would
really appreciate it. My printer
is a Seikosha SP-1900.

On the future of OUTLET, person-
ally I would prefer an increase
in price rather than a bi-
monthly disk and I agree with
you that contributors to OUTLET
are happy just to share their
work. However, programmers who
would like payment could have
reviews written for them in
OUTLET plus a sample of their
program. Then any individual
requiring that program could
write to them direct.

Whatever you decide to do I will
support OUTLET. I wish you all
the best for the future to get
over these hard times.

       Yours sincerely,

           J. Livett

Brian Cavers to T.J. Livett

I must have another go at BULLY
although I'm curious about your
pressing the RESET button "very
quickly"! I must give it a go.

There is no printer routine for
PFN. Probably what you want is
the DTP package WORDMASTER etc.
I'm told PCG, the supplier, are
now trading as POLYTYPE. Ring
them on 0229 832807 weekday
mornings only. The whole package
is over `30 though but it is a
full wordprocessor, graphics and
text style editor and printer.

                       - Brian

Brian Cavers to Graham Yeardley

I'm glad the ROM INDEX prints
out perfectly on your +3. This
contrasts with Phil Parnell's
experience -he is getting triple
line feeds! My own +3 does not
need the POKEs at all and I
wonder if there is yet a third
version of the +3 that needs
slightly different POKEs?

Our own routines at lines 1001
and 1002 in every OUTLET loader
(this is the file called "DISK"
on a +3; RESET and MERGE "DISK"
to examine it) are as follows...
 23354,62: 23355,16 : 23388,16:
 23399,20: 23404,203: 23405,37:
plus a complete routine from
23438 to 23459. I forget what
they all do!

Note that as well as the extra
ones, our differs from yours in
that we POKE 23399,20 whereas
you POKE 23399,16 - a misprint?

The +3 versions of OUTLET began
at Issue 23. The tape version
will not transfer and run on +3
disc though individual programs
may.

The +3 OUTDEX main file is on
OUTLET EXTRA 1 - at the same
price as OUTLET.

                         - Brian

From: Malcolm Perry,
      216 Marlpool Lane,
      KIDDERMINSTER DY11 5DL

Dear Brian and Ron,

LC10 printer problems.

I have had the LC10 for about 3
years and I am now on my third
print head. I am wondering if
any other users of LC10 ( or
STAR printer) have experienced
any problems.

In all my cases, while the
symptoms of missing part of
characters could be put down to
a sticking pin, it is in fact
due to a break in the ribbon
cable feeding the print head.

The faults in my cases have been
characterized by only missing
bits when the head is towards
the right hand side and this is
when the cable is bent at its
sharpest under the print head
carriage.

It's also more than coincidence,
I consider, that each time the
break has been at a point where
there is a sharp corner or edge
on the plastic moulding of the
head carriage that presses into
the cable. I did put it to STAR
as a possible design point but
they said they were not aware of
any design or previous problems.

I have also had correspondence
with another LC10 user who had

problems. He had been told by a
service agent, after a
discussion with Star, that Star
had said that a few machines
were not finished off properly
and the rough edges could lead
to cable failure. Star, however,
said they were not aware of any
such problem and were surprised
at the service agent's comment.

I, on my part, have been filing
down sharp corners as they come
to light and Star have so far,
while denying a problem, been
replacing faulty heads "with
compliments" even though the
machine is now well out of
guarantee. They also asked for
faulty heads back for
inspection.

It might be of interest that I
was told cable was not available
separately as it was soldered
onto the head but the latest
heads have plug in cables so
they may now be supplied on
their own.

If anyone has had what they
consider to be early failure or
problems like mine, drop me a
line and I will give the name
and address of the person I
dealt with at Star - mind you, I
cannot guarantee or say that
Star will follow up as in my
case.

Malcolm Perry

From: A. Morgan,47 Barr Crescent
    INVERKEITHING, FIFE KY11 1DW


Dear Ron,

Since I last wrote I have been
saving my pennies and have now
got a Star LC-200 colour printer
plus an old Q.L. that no one
wanted.So,if anyone has software
for the QL I would like to hear
from them.

Do you know anyone who can
repair my Brother M1109?

           Alex Morgan

Brian Cavers to Alex Morgan


No, I don't know of any repair
company for printers. I think
the thing to do is contact your
supplier. They may send it back
to the manufacturer for repair.

                         Brian.

## Letters (1)

September, 1992   Page Reply

How to write to us...02     - John Hall............03    06 Phil Parnell.........07    17 Vincent L. Jacks.....25    30 T.J. Livett..........37    40 Graham Yeardley......41    43 Malcolm Perry........45     - Alex Morgan..........49    50

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters.
